title: Barre Chord: Efficient Virtual Memory Translation for Multi-Chip-Module GPUs
problem: Virtual memory translation in multi-chip-module GPUs creates a critical bottleneck due to limited IOMMU parallelism when handling concurrent address translation requests across many GPU threads. This limits scalable performance in MCM GPU architectures.
motivation: Multi-chip-module GPUs are essential for continued performance scaling as Moore's law ends, but their high concurrency demands efficient and scalable virtual memory translation.
method: Barre Chord batches virtual address translations (mapping program memory addresses to actual hardware locations) by grouping GPU threads that execute together—called coalescing groups. When threads in a group access nearby memory, the system translates just one address fully, then uses simple arithmetic to find where the others map, skipping expensive page table lookups (called page table walks). F-Barre extends this by sharing grouping information between chiplets within a multi-chip GPU and intelligently expanding groups when addresses are stored next to each other in memory.
key_novelty: Exploiting the natural tendency of GPU thread groups to access nearby memory locations together—a property called coalescing—to batch virtual address translations and eliminate redundant page table lookups.
contributions: Identifies IOMMU parallelism as critical bottleneck for MCM GPU performance and scalability
Proposes Barre mechanism for coalescing-group-based virtual address translation
Introduces F-Barre for intra-MCM translation through chiplet coordination and information sharing
Achieves 1.36x speedup average (2.09x with expansion) with only 4.22% area overhead
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: virtual memory translation for multi-chip GPUs
